symbols.description: A molecule that contains biological instructions and is passed from adult organisms to offspring during reproduction.
symbols.name: Deoxyribonucleic acid

symbols.description: Instructions contained in DNA that make each species unique and can be used to make proteins and for other biological processes.
symbols.name: biological instructions

symbols.description: A biological grouping whose uniqueness is associated with the instructions contained in DNA.
symbols.name: species

symbols.description: An organism that can pass DNA to its offspring during reproduction.
symbols.name: adult organism

symbols.description: An organism that receives DNA from adult organisms during reproduction.
symbols.name: offspring

symbols.description: An organism in which DNA is found inside a nucleus.
symbols.name: eukaryote

symbols.description: A small biological structure that contains DNA and, in the described organisms, may contain a nucleus and mitochondria.
symbols.name: cell

symbols.description: A special area of a cell in which DNA is found in eukaryotes.
symbols.name: nucleus

symbols.description: The tightly packaged form of a DNA molecule, present during cell division to enable transfer to new cells.
symbols.name: chromosome

symbols.description: A process during which DNA unwinds so it can be copied.
symbols.name: DNA replication

symbols.description: The process in which DNA becomes unwound for copying or for use of its instructions.
symbols.name: DNA unwinding

symbols.description: The cycle during which DNA may unwind at times other than DNA replication.
symbols.name: cell cycle

symbols.description: The making of proteins using DNA instructions.
symbols.name: protein production

symbols.description: A process during which DNA is in compact chromosome form to enable transfer to new cells.
symbols.name: cell division

symbols.description: DNA found in the nucleus of a cell.
symbols.name: nuclear DNA

symbols.description: An organism's complete set of nuclear DNA.
symbols.name: genome

symbols.description: A cell structure containing a small amount of DNA in humans and other complex organisms and generating energy needed for the cell to function properly.
symbols.name: mitochondrion

symbols.description: Energy generated by mitochondria that the cell needs to function properly.
symbols.name: cellular energy

symbols.description: A form of reproduction in which organisms inherit nuclear DNA from a male parent and a female parent.
symbols.name: sexual reproduction

symbols.description: The parent from which an organism inherits half of its nuclear DNA in sexual reproduction.
symbols.name: male parent

symbols.description: The parent from which an organism inherits half of its nuclear DNA and all of its mitochondrial DNA in sexual reproduction.
symbols.name: female parent

symbols.description: DNA located in mitochondria and inherited from the female parent in the described sexual reproduction.
symbols.name: mitochondrial DNA

symbols.description: A cell that keeps its mitochondria during fertilization.
symbols.name: egg cell

symbols.description: A cell that does not keep its mitochondria during fertilization.
symbols.name: sperm cell

symbols.description: The process during which only egg cells, and not sperm cells, keep their mitochondria in the described inheritance pattern.
symbols.name: fertilization

symbols.description: A chemical building block of DNA made of a phosphate group, a sugar group, and one of four types of nitrogen bases.
symbols.name: nucleotide

symbols.description: One of the three parts of a nucleotide.
symbols.name: phosphate group

symbols.description: One of the three parts of a nucleotide.
symbols.name: sugar group

symbols.description: One of four types of chemical parts in a nucleotide.
symbols.name: nitrogen base

symbols.description: A strand formed when nucleotides are linked into a chain, with phosphate and sugar groups alternating.
symbols.name: DNA strand

symbols.description: One of the four types of nitrogen bases found in DNA nucleotides.
symbols.name: adenine

symbols.name: thymine

propositions.statement: DNA is passed from adult organisms to offspring during reproduction.
Mitochondrial DNA is inherited by offspring from the female parent.

relationships.statement: Biological instructions are contained in DNA.
DNA is passed from adult organisms to their offspring during reproduction.
The nucleus is a special area inside the cell.
In eukaryotes, DNA is found inside the nucleus.
A chromosome is the tightly packaged form of a DNA molecule.
DNA unwinding occurs during DNA replication.
DNA unwinds so that its instructions can be used to make proteins.
During cell division, DNA is in its compact chromosome form to enable transfer to new cells.
DNA found in the nucleus is called nuclear DNA.
An organism's complete set of nuclear DNA is called its genome.
Mitochondria are cell structures.
A small amount of DNA is located in mitochondria.
Mitochondria generate the energy the cell needs to function properly.
Humans are identified as complex organisms.
In sexual reproduction, organisms inherit nuclear DNA from the male parent and the female parent.
Organisms inherit all of their mitochondrial DNA from the female parent.
Egg cells keep their mitochondria during fertilization, which retain mitochondrial DNA.
DNA is made of nucleotides.
A phosphate group is one of the three parts of a nucleotide.
A sugar group is one of the three parts of a nucleotide.
A nitrogen base is one of the three parts of a nucleotide.
Nucleotides are linked into chains to form a DNA strand.
Adenine is one of the four types of nitrogen bases found in nucleotides.
Thymine is one of the four types of nitrogen bases found in nucleotides.
Guanine is one of the four types of nitrogen bases found in nucleotides.
Cytosine is one of the four types of nitrogen bases found in nucleotides.
The order, or sequence, of nitrogen bases determines which biological instructions are contained in a DNA strand.
Genes are included in the human genome.

IS_A [STRUCTURAL; direction=instance_to_type]

  roles: source=part or component; target=containing whole

  avoid: Never reverse whole and part; do not use for interaction or dependency.
